about.title: San Juan Bautista Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: San Juan Bautista is a small place, with fewer than two thousand residents, and a loss here is felt by nearly everyone in town. In 2025 the city recorded five injury collisions and no traffic deaths, which is a relief in the numbers but no comfort to a family whose loved one died elsewhere in San Benito County, on a work site, in a hospital, or on a property that was not kept safe. Public records show most local crashes cluster along SR-156, Route 156 westbound and The Alameda, often on Sunday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. A wrongful death claim is a civil matter, separate from any criminal charges or coroner's findings. It lets a spouse, domestic partner, children, or in some cases dependent heirs seek payment for funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter if a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm; we simply connect you, for free, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in San Juan Bautista Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to the spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can explain where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: The clock matters
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to bring a claim, and the window is shorter when a city, county or state agency is involved. Early guidance keeps a preventable deadline from closing the door.

items.title: A civil claim, handled separately
items.desc: Whether or not a criminal case is opened, a wrongful death action moves on its own track and covers funeral expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of companionship and guidance. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on SR-156 outside San Juan Bautista. Does it matter that it was not inside city limits?
items.answer: No. Wrongful death claims are governed by California law, not by city boundaries. What matters is who was at fault and whether the responsible party was a private driver, a business, or a government entity, since that last category carries a shorter filing deadline. An independent attorney can sort out jurisdiction and timing for you.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: You do not have to wait. A wrongful death lawsuit is a civil action and proceeds independently of any criminal prosecution. Criminal cases can take a long time, and the two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless, so it is wise to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm, and what will this cost us?
items.answer: LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects grieving families with an independent personal injury attorney who handles wrongful death cases. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless they recover compensation for you.
